focus: 〜たとたん(に) vs 〜(か)と思うと
sentence: 私は疲れてベッドに（　　）、すぐに深い眠りに落ちてしまった。
translation: Exhausted, the instant I got into bed, I fell fast asleep.
ruleTitle: 1課-3: 〜たとたん(に) — the instant that ~
explanation:
Correct: [2] 入ったとたんに (動 た形 ＋ とたん).
Means: you did an action, and immediately after, an unexpected or involuntary event happened. Crucially, it CAN be used for the speaker's own action (falling asleep, feeling dizzy).
trap:
⚠️ The Speaker Action Ban:
• [1] 〜(か)と思うと is BANNED for the speaker's own intentional actions (✗ 私は座ったかと思うと...). It is only for observing someone else or nature.
• [3] 〜にあたって is for a deliberate, special positive milestone (opening a shop, starting life).
• [4] 〜最中に means 'in the middle of', interrupted by a surprise.

focus: 〜に際して vs 〜にあたって
sentence: 今回の入院（　　）、同僚たちが温かい励ましの言葉をかけてくれた。
translation: On the occasion of my hospitalization, my colleagues gave me warm words of encouragement.
ruleTitle: 1課-2: 〜に際して・〜にあたって — on the occasion of ~
explanation:
Correct: [1] に際して (名 ＋ に際して).
Both mean 'on the occasion of', but 〜にあたって strictly refuses negative-image words (✗ 別れにあたって, ✗ 入院にあたって, ✗ 倒産にあたって). It must be positive and forward-looking.
〜に際して is neutral and accepts both positive and negative occasions.
trap:
⚠️ The Negative Word Ban:
• [2] にあたって refuses negative words. Since 入院 (hospitalization) is an illness/setback, only に際して is allowed.
• [3] かと思うと requires verb た形.
• [4] 最中に would imply they interrupted the act of checking in.

focus: 〜か〜ないかのうちに
sentence: 終了のチャイムが（　　）、学生たちは一斉に教室から出ていった。
translation: Almost before the end chime had finished ringing, the students stormed out of the classroom all at once.
choices: 鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに
ruleTitle: 1課-5: 〜か〜ないかのうちに — almost before ~ had finished
explanation:
Correct: [1] 鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに (動 辞書形/た形 ＋ か ＋ 動 ない形 ＋ かのうちに).
Means: at the very split-second ~ finishes (almost zero time gap), the next event happens. Connects to momentary change verbs (鳴る, 終わる, 着く).
trap:
⚠️ Zero Time-Gap Rule:
• [2] 鳴りつつあるうちに is grammatically broken (つつある + うちに).
• [3] 鳴った上で means 'after doing A as preparation for step B', not instant simultaneity.
• [4] 鳴るばかりに doesn't fit this meaning.

focus: 〜最中に（割り込み妨害）
sentence: 大事な商談を行っている（　　）、突然携帯電話が大音量で鳴り響いた。
translation: Right in the middle of conducting an important business negotiation, a phone suddenly rang out loudly.
ruleTitle: 2課-1: 〜最中だ — right in the middle of ~
explanation:
Correct: [1] 最中に (動 ている形 ＋ 最中に).
Means: right in the middle of an action of relatively short duration. The signature exam pattern: it is followed by an unplanned interruption or nuisance that breaks in.
trap:
⚠️ The Interruption Nuance:
• [3] うちに means 'while / before the window closes', not an abrupt disruptive interruption.
• [2] つつ means 'while doing A, doing B' (requires the same subject doing both actions!).
• [4] 次第 means 'as soon as', followed by intention.

focus: 〜うちに (A: 期限・意志動作)
sentence: せっかく日本に留学しているのだから、日本に（　　）、できるだけ多くの観光地を訪れたい。
translation: Since I have this rare chance to study in Japan, while I'm still here (before the opportunity passes), I want to visit as many tourist spots as possible.
ruleTitle: 2課-2: 〜うちに — do it before the window closes
explanation:
Correct: [1] いるうちに.
Meaning A of 〜うちに: there is a time window; before the state changes, seize the chance to do something. The clause after is VOLITIONAL (〜たい, 〜よう, 〜てください).
trap:
⚠️ The Volition Split (うちに A vs B):
• うちに (A = window of opportunity) TAKES volitional endings (訪れたい = I want to visit).
• うちに (B = unintended change) REFUSES volition (外が暗くなってきた = it grew dark).
• [2] いたとたんに means 'the instant I was', which makes no sense with a long stay.

focus: 〜つつある vs 〜(よ)うとしている
sentence: 医師たちの懸命な治療により、患者の容体は少しずつ（　　）。
translation: Thanks to the doctors' devoted treatment, the patient's condition is gradually in the process of recovering.
choices: 回復しようとしている
ruleTitle: 2課-5: 〜つつある — is in the process of ~ing
explanation:
Correct: [1] 回復しつつある (動 ます-stem ＋ つつある).
Means: the change is currently underway in progress (formal/stiff). Naturally matches gradual adverbs like 少しずつ (little by little).
trap:
⚠️ Before vs During the Change:
• [2] 回復しようとしている means 'is just ABOUT to start recovering' (before the change starts). Doesn't fit with 少しずつ (gradually).
• [3] 回復する一方だ implies relentless momentum, usually used for worsening trends.

focus: 〜一方だ (一方向への変化)
sentence: 最近の円安の影響で、輸入品の価格は（　　）、家計への負担が増えている。
translation: Due to the recent weak yen, the prices of imported goods just keep rising, and the burden on households is increasing.
ruleTitle: 2課-3: 〜一方だ・〜ばかりだ — just keeps ~ing
explanation:
Correct: [1] 上がる一方だ (動 辞書形 ＋ 一方だ).
Means: a change keeps continuously advancing in one single direction without stopping (very often a worsening situation).
trap:
⚠️ One-Way Trajectory:
• [2] 上がりつつ is mid-clause and needs a main clause predicate.
• [3] 上がった上で means 'after prices rise as preparation...'
• [4] 上がろうとしている means 'are on the verge of rising', but they are already rising.

focus: 〜てはじめて (新しい気づき)
sentence: 大きな病気を（　　）、健康の本当のありがたさに気づくことができた。
translation: Only after experiencing a serious illness was I able to realize the true value of good health.
ruleTitle: 3課-1: 〜てはじめて — only after ~ did I realize...
explanation:
Correct: [1] 経験してはじめて (動 て形 ＋ はじめて).
Means: only after going through this experience did a new awareness dawn that was previously impossible. Followed by realization verbs: 気づく, わかる, 実感する.
trap:
⚠️ Realization vs Planned Action:
• [2] 〜上で requires a deliberate, volitional next action (✗ 上で気づいた is wrong; you cannot plan a realization).
• [4] 〜て以来 means 'ever since, state continued unbroken', but doesn't express the sudden awakening.

focus: 〜上(で) (準備ステップ→意志動作)
sentence: 契約内容の詳細を十分に確認（　　）、こちらの書類にご署名をお願いいたします。
translation: Please sign this document after checking the contract details thoroughly first.
ruleTitle: 3課-2: 〜上(で) — after ~ing (as preparation)
explanation:
Correct: [1] の上で (名 −の ＋ 上で).
Means: do step A first as deliberate preparation, then take volitional step B. Both actions share the same subject, and step A informs step B.
trap:
⚠️ Sequential Step vs Stacking:
• Do NOT confuse with 〜上に (Ch 6) which means 'on top of that / in addition to'.
• [3] 次第 attaches to verb ます-stem (確認し次第), not noun + の.
• [4] に限って means 'of all days/things'.

focus: 〜次第 (〜したらすぐ・意志必須・過去形禁止)
sentence: 詳しい日程が（　　）、改めてメールにてご連絡申し上げます。
translation: As soon as the detailed schedule is decided, I will contact you again by email.
ruleTitle: 3課-3: 〜次第 — as soon as ~
explanation:
Correct: [1] 決まり次第 (動 ます-stem ＋ 次第).
Means: the moment ~ happens, immediately do the next action. Formal/business style. Followed by speaker's intention (ご連絡申し上げます) or urging (〜てください).
trap:
⚠️ The Past Tense Ban:
• 〜次第 CANNOT have a past tense ending (✗ 決まり次第、連絡しました is illegal).
• [2] 決まったとたん is followed by an unexpected event, and bans speaker's intentional actions like ご連絡申し上げます.

focus: 〜てからでないと (後ろは必ず否定文)
sentence: 上司の許可を（　　）、この予算を使用することはできません。
translation: Unless you obtain your supervisor's permission first, you cannot use this budget.
ruleTitle: 3課-5: 〜てからでないと — unless you ~ first
explanation:
Correct: [1] 取ってからでないと (動 て形 ＋ からでないと).
Means: unless you do A first, B cannot happen. The sentence ending MUST be negative (〜ない, 〜できない, 〜無理だ).
trap:
⚠️ Mandatory Negative Ending:
• The final predicate is できません (cannot). This is the hallmark signature of 〜てからでないと.
• [2] 取った上で would require a positive action (e.g. 使用してください).

focus: 〜からして (些細な例を挙げて不満・批判)
sentence: あの会社は、面接官の（　　）非常に高圧的で、第一印象から悪かった。
translation: At that company, just the interviewer's attitude alone was extremely overbearing — the first impression was terrible from the start.
ruleTitle: 4課-2: 〜からして — judging from just ~ alone
explanation:
Correct: [1] 態度からして (名 ＋ からして).
Means: take just this one small detail — even that is so, therefore the whole thing must be bad too. Followed by a negative evaluation or complaint.
trap:
⚠️ Complaint vs Representative Group:
• [2] 〜をはじめ is neutral and introduces the leading member of a group (校長をはじめ先生方 = teachers, starting with the principal). Not for complaints.
• [3] 〜を通して means 'via an intermediary'.

focus: 〜にわたって (空間・時間の大きな幅)
sentence: 台風の影響による大雨は、広範囲に（　　）甚大な被害をもたらした。
translation: The heavy rain from the typhoon caused immense damage spanning across a wide area.
ruleTitle: 4課-3: 〜にわたって — spanning across ~
explanation:
Correct: [1] わたって (名 ＋ にわたって).
Means: extending across an entire large range. Attaches to nouns of large spatial scale (広範囲), long time periods (3年間), or large numbers of times.
trap:
⚠️ Scale Requirement:
• Must have substantial width/scale (広範囲にわたって, 長年にわたって). Tiny intervals (✗ 5分にわたって) are impossible.

focus: 〜を通して / 〜を通じて (仲介・媒介)
sentence: 彼とは直接面識がなかったため、共通の友人（　　）連絡を取った。
translation: Since I had no direct acquaintance with him, I contacted him through a mutual friend.
ruleTitle: 4課-4: 〜を通じて・〜を通して — via; through an intermediary
explanation:
Correct: [1] を通して (名 ＋ を通して).
Means: using ~ as an intermediary person or medium to achieve a goal. Cannot be a direct physical tool in your hand (you write with a pen [で], but contact someone through a friend [を通して]).
trap:
⚠️ Intermediary vs Direct Tool:
• Indirect mediator = を通して / を通じて.
• [2] をもとに means 'based on as raw material'.
• [4] をめぐって means 'over/concerning a dispute'.

focus: 〜に限り (公式告知・例外の限定)
sentence: 本日の夕方6時（　　）、全品20パーセント引きのタイムセールを実施いたします。
translation: Today until 6 PM only, we are holding a 20% off flash sale on all items.
ruleTitle: 5課-1: 〜に限り — only ~ (as an official exception)
explanation:
Correct: [1] に限り (名 ＋ に限り).
Means: only ~ is special; only ~ is the exception. Stiff/formal public announcement style used by shops, notices, hospitals.
trap:
⚠️ Official Notice vs Murphy's Law:
• [2] 〜に限って is used for complaints about bad luck timing ('on the very day when...').
• [1] 〜に限り is the public rule exception ('Today only').
• [3] 〜に限らず means 'not limited to'.

focus: 〜限りでは (情報源の限定・断定回避)
sentence: 私の（　　）限りでは、そのような方針の変更はまだ正式に発表されていません。
translation: As far as I know, no such policy change has been officially announced yet.
ruleTitle: 5課-3: 〜限りでは — as far as ~ (goes / tells us)
explanation:
Correct: [1] 知っている (動 ている形 ＋ 限りでは).
Means: if we limit the source of information to ~, this is what can be said. Used to hedge a statement carefully.
trap:
⚠️ Information Verbs Only:
• Attaches strictly to info-getting verbs: 知っている, 調べた, 聞いた, 見た.
• '知っている限りでは' (as far as I know) and '調べた限りでは' (as far as my investigation shows) are exam staples.

focus: 〜に限って (マーフィーの法則・不運の重なり)
sentence: 傘を持っていない日に（　　）、決まって激しい雨が降ってくる。
translation: Precisely on days when I don't have an umbrella, without fail it pours.
ruleTitle: 5課-4: 〜に限って — of all days / Murphy's Law
explanation:
Correct: [1] 限って (名 ＋ に限って).
Means: of all times, precisely on this occasion, something unlucky coincides, causing speaker frustration.
trap:
⚠️ The 3 Faces of 〜に限って:
• ① Coinciding bad luck (急いでいる日に限って電車が遅れる = Murphy's Law).
• ② Different from usual (今日に限ってよく喋る).
• ③ Misplaced trust (彼に限って嘘をつくはずがない).

focus: 〜ばかりか (エスカレーション・それどころかもっと)
sentence: 彼は無断で仕事を休んだ（　　）、連絡すら取ろうとしなかった。
translation: Not only did he skip work without notice, he didn't even try to contact us.
ruleTitle: 6課-3: 〜ばかりか — not only ~, but even ~
explanation:
Correct: [1] ばかりか (普通形 ＋ ばかりか).
Means: Clause 1 is already abnormal/shocking, and Clause 2 escalates with something even more extreme. Often accompanied by も, まで, or すら.
trap:
⚠️ Escalation Factor:
• [2] うえで means 'after doing A as preparation for B'.
• [3] 次第 means 'as soon as'.
• [4] からして takes a noun, not a verb clause.

focus: 〜上(に) (同方向の評価の積み重ね)
sentence: このパソコンは性能が優れている（　　）、デザインも洗練されていて使いやすい。
translation: Not only does this PC have superb performance, its design is sleek and easy to use on top of that.
ruleTitle: 6課-5: 〜上(に) — on top of that / in addition
explanation:
Correct: [1] 上に (普通形 ＋ 上に).
Means: stacks multiple traits of the SAME polarity (Positive + Positive, or Negative + Negative). Good specs (優れている) + Good design (洗練されている).
trap:
⚠️ Polarity Rule & 〜上で vs 〜上に:
• 〜上に CANNOT combine opposite polarities (✗ 安い上にまずい is illegal).
• 〜上で (Ch 3) = sequence (do A first, then B). 〜上に (Ch 6) = additive stacking.

focus: 〜をめぐって (複数者による争い・対立)
sentence: 新工場の建設予定地を（　　）、住民と行政の間で対立が続いている。
translation: Over the planned construction site of the new factory, conflict continues between residents and the government.
ruleTitle: 7課-2: 〜をめぐって — over; surrounding (a dispute)
explanation:
Correct: [1] めぐって (名 ＋ をめぐって).
Means: conflict, dispute, or debate over an issue. The subjects MUST be PLURAL (residents and administration), followed by verbs of conflict/debate: 対立する, 争う, 議論する.
trap:
⚠️ The Plural Conflict Requirement:
• Must involve multiple parties in conflict. If only one person is acting, 〜をめぐって is wrong.
• [2] に関して is a neutral theme for collecting info, not mutual dispute.

focus: 〜にかけては (特定の能力・技術で右に出る者はいない)
sentence: 味の繊細な見分け方（　　）、あの料理長の右に出る者はいない。
translation: When it comes to distinguishing subtle flavors, nobody surpasses that head chef.
ruleTitle: 7課-3: 〜にかけては — when it comes to ~ (nobody beats them)
explanation:
Correct: [1] にかけては (名 ＋ にかけては).
Means: in the domain of this specific skill/technique, this person is unmatched. Followed by supreme praise: 誰にも負けない, 右に出る者はいない, 一番だ.
trap:
⚠️ Skills & Unmatched Praise:
• Before: MUST be a skill or ability (見分け方, 記憶力, 早さ). Not a general topic.
• After: MUST be highest praise ('nobody beats them').

focus: 〜にこたえて (期待や要望に応じる)
sentence: 地元ファンの熱烈な応援（　　）、選手たちは見事な逆転勝利を収めた。
translation: In response to the passionate cheers of the local fans, the players clinched a splendid comeback victory.
ruleTitle: 7課-5: 〜にこたえて — in response to (expectations/cheers)
explanation:
Correct: [1] にこたえて (名 ＋ にこたえて).
Means: acting so as to fulfill someone's expectations, wishes, or requests. Attaches to: 応援, 期待, 要望, 希望, アンコール.
trap:
⚠️ The Request/Expectation Nouns:
• Strictly limited to expectations/demands (期待, 要望, 応援). Not for general objects.
• [2] に対して means 'attitude directed toward a target'.

focus: 〜のに対して (明確な対比・対照)
sentence: 兄が社交的で友人が多いの（　　）、弟は物静かで読書を好む。
translation: Whereas the older brother is sociable and has many friends, in contrast the younger brother is quiet and likes reading.
ruleTitle: 7課-4: 〜に対して — in contrast to (Meaning B)
explanation:
Correct: [1] に対して (普通形 ＋ の ＋ に対して).
Meaning B of 〜に対して: indicates a sharp, explicit contrast between two subjects. The nominalizing の before に対して is the grammatical signal.
trap:
⚠️ Target vs Contrast:
• Meaning A (toward a target): 目上の人に対して (no の).
• Meaning B (in contrast to): 兄が〜なのに対して (has の, comparing two distinct subjects).

focus: 〜をもとに vs 〜に基づいて (創作・新開発)
sentence: この映画は、実際に起きた未解決事件を（　　）制作されたフィクションである。
translation: This movie is a work of fiction created based on an actual unsolved incident.
ruleTitle: 8課-1: 〜をもとに(して) — based on (as raw material)
explanation:
Correct: [1] もとにして (名 ＋ をもとに).
Means: creating something new (a movie, novel, design, product) out of ~ as foundation/source material. Usually followed by creation verbs: 制作する, 作る, 開発する.
trap:
⚠️ 〜をもとに vs 〜に基づいて:
• 〜をもとに = makes something NEW out of data/story (films, products, art).
• 〜に基づいて = judges or acts ACCORDING to an established criterion or law (court ruling, policy decision).
• [3] 沿って = follows a continuous path/rule like a flow.

focus: 〜のもとで vs 〜のもとに (人＝で / 状況＝に)
sentence: 厳しい指導で知られる名監督の（　　）、選手たちは毎日の猛練習に励んでいる。
translation: Under the famed coach known for strict guidance, the players devote themselves to fierce daily training.
ruleTitle: 8課-4: 〜のもとで・〜のもとに — under ~
explanation:
Correct: [1] もとで (名 ＋ のもとで).
Attaches mainly to PERSON words (監督, 先生, 両親) meaning 'under that person's influence/guidance'. Followed by action verbs: 励む, 学ぶ, 暮らす.
trap:
⚠️ Person vs Condition Rule (Exam Gold):
• Person noun → 〜のもとで (監督のもとで学ぶ).
• Condition/situation noun → 〜のもとに (全員の了解のもとに決定された / 厳重な管理のもとに保存されている).

focus: 〜に沿って (マニュアル・方針の流れに従う)
sentence: 業務の混乱を防ぐため、作業は必ず安全マニュアル（　　）進めてください。
translation: To prevent operational confusion, please be sure to carry out the work strictly in line with the safety manual.
ruleTitle: 8課-3: 〜に沿って — in line with; along (guidelines/path)
explanation:
Correct: [1] に沿って (名 ＋ に沿って).
Means: acting so as to follow ~ (rules, manuals, guidelines, expectations) continuously without straying from it, like moving along a track.
trap:
⚠️ Flowing Along a Guideline:
• Attaches to standard words: マニュアル, 方針, ルール, 計画.
• Unlike 〜に基づいて (a single fixed anchor), 〜に沿って emphasizes an ongoing continuous flow along the path.

focus: 〜向け vs 〜向き (専用設計 vs たまたま適する)
sentence: このプログラミング入門書は、専門用語を避けてIT初学者（　　）分かりやすく書かれている。
translation: This introductory programming book avoids technical jargon and is written clearly aimed specifically at IT beginners.
ruleTitle: 8課-5: 〜向けだ — aimed at; designed for
explanation:
Correct: [1] 向けに (名 ＋ 向けに).
Means: deliberately designed, manufactured, or authored specifically for that target audience (IT beginners, children, tourists).
trap:
⚠️ Made FOR vs Happening to SUIT:
• 〜向け = deliberately made FOR that specific group (初心者向けの本).
• 〜向き = happens to SUIT that group naturally (この仕事は初心者向きだ = happens to suit beginners).

focus: 〜につれて (一方向の自然変化・意志禁止)
sentence: 台風が列島に（　　）、次第に風雨が強まり波も高くなってきた。
translation: As the typhoon approached the archipelago, the wind and rain gradually intensified and the waves grew higher.
ruleTitle: 9課-1: 〜につれて — as ~ progresses in tandem
explanation:
Correct: [1] 近づくにつれて (動 辞書形 ＋ につれて).
Means: as one phenomenon advances, another naturally shifts in tandem. Used with gradual change verbs (近づく, 進む, 上がる).
trap:
⚠️ One-Directional & Natural Phenomena Only:
• 〜につれて is only for one-directional progression.
• BANNED after 〜につれて: The speaker's volitional intention or urging sentences (✗ につれて、避難しよう). It must describe natural changes.

focus: 〜次第だ vs 〜次第 (名詞＝次第だ / 動詞＝次第)
sentence: 入社試験に合格できるかどうかは、今後の筆記試験と面接の（　　）。
translation: Whether you pass the employment exam or not depends entirely on the results of the upcoming written exam and interview.
ruleTitle: 9課-3: 〜次第だ — depends on ~
explanation:
Correct: [1] 結果次第だ (名 ＋ 次第だ).
Means: whether X happens is determined by and depends on ~ (effort, weather, results).
trap:
⚠️ 3課 vs 9課 次第:
• Noun ＋ 次第だ (Ch 9) = 'depends on ~' (努力次第だ, 天気次第だ).
• Verb ます-stem ＋ 次第 (Ch 3) = 'as soon as ~' (決まり次第ご連絡します).

focus: 〜に応じて vs 〜にこたえて (可変数量 vs 期待・要望)
sentence: お客様の年齢や（　　）、最適な保険プランをご提案いたします。
translation: We will propose the optimal insurance plan matched to our clients' age and budget.
ruleTitle: 9課-4: 〜に応じて — in accordance with a variable
explanation:
Correct: [1] ご予算に応じて (名 ＋ に応じて).
Means: adapting or varying something to match a flexible quantity (budget, age, fitness, income).
trap:
⚠️ Variable Quantity vs Expectation/Request:
• 〜に応じて matches a variable number/scale (予算, 体力, 年齢).
• 〜にこたえて (Ch 7-5) answers someone's hope/request (期待, 要望, アンコール).

focus: 〜につけて (心の動き・自然とそう感じる)
sentence: 学生時代のアルバムを（　　）、仲間たちと過ごした懐かしい日々を思い出す。
translation: Every time I look at my school album, I remember with fondness the days spent with my friends.
ruleTitle: 9課-5: 〜につけて — every time ~, I feel...
explanation:
Correct: [1] 見るにつけて (動 辞書形 ＋ につけて).
Means: whenever I do ~, that specific emotional reaction or memory is naturally evoked. Followed by emotion/heart verbs: 思い出す, 心配になる, 反省する.
trap:
⚠️ Movement of the Heart:
• The predicate MUST express a feeling or recollection (思い出す, 心配になる), not a deliberate action.
• Idiom: 何かにつけて = 'every time anything happens / at every opportunity'.

focus: 〜やら〜やら (収拾がつかない・大変さ)
sentence: 今週は引っ越しの荷造りを（　　）、役所で手続きをする（　　）で、息つく暇もなかった。
translation: This week was complete chaos what with packing boxes for the move and doing procedures at the city office — I didn't even have time to catch my breath.
choices: するというか／するというか
するにせよ／するにせよ
するといった／するといった
ruleTitle: 10課-1: 〜やら〜やら — what with ~ and ~ (overwhelmed/messy)
explanation:
Correct: [1] するやら／するやら (動 辞書形/名/イ形 ＋ やら).
Means: there is A and B and all sorts of things going on. Expresses that things are chaotic, untidy, and overwhelmingly busy/exhausting.
trap:
⚠️ Chaotic Multiplicity & Exhaustion:
• 〜やら〜やら emphasizes that situations are disorganized and hard to keep tidy, with a sense of fatigue or burden (息つく暇もない, 大変だった).

focus: 〜というか〜というか (二つの評価・判断保留)
sentence: 彼の歯に衣着せぬ発言は、率直（　　）無礼（　　）、聞く人によって受け止め方が分かれる。
translation: His unvarnished remarks are honest, or perhaps rude — people's reactions vary depending on who is listening.
ruleTitle: 10課-2: 〜というか〜というか — whether to call it ~ or ~
explanation:
Correct: [1] というか／というか (普通形 ＋ というか).
Means: you could describe the situation as A, or you could equally call it B. The speaker is thinking aloud or hedging because neither label alone fits perfectly.
trap:
⚠️ Two Expressions for ONE Situation:
• Gives two different interpretations of the exact same event or person (率直 vs 無礼, 安心した vs 寂しい).

focus: 〜にせよ〜にせよ (対比・話者の判断や忠告)
sentence: 提案に（　　）、会議で責任を持って自分の意見の根拠を説明すべきだ。
translation: Whether you agree or disagree with the proposal, you ought to explain the basis of your opinion responsibly at the meeting.
choices: 賛成するにせよ反対するにせよ
賛成するやら反対するやら
賛成するにつれて反対するにつれて
賛成するばかりか反対するばかりか
ruleTitle: 10課-3: 〜にしても〜にしても・〜にせよ〜にせよ — whether A or B
explanation:
Correct: [1] 賛成するにせよ反対するにせよ (動 辞書形 ＋ にせよ).
Means: whether you take case A or opposing case B, the exact same principle, advice, or necessity applies. Followed by speaker's judgment: 〜べきだ, 〜必要がある.
trap:
⚠️ Opposing Cases + Advice/Principle:
• Lists opposing alternatives (賛成／反対, 行く／行かない).
• 〜にせよ〜にせよ is the stiffest/most formal variation of 〜にしても〜にしても.
